query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled aging heat treatment applied as a post-solidification thermal processing step can promote the precipitation of secondary phases at lamellar interfaces, thereby enhancing both strength and ductility while also improving thermal and corrosion stability for AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy fastener alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar eutectic microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy in the as-solidified condition with mechanical properties below industrial requirements.
generation.intervention: A two-step heat treatment consisting of a high-temperature solution treatment followed by an aging step. For example, solutionize at ~1100°C for a short time to homogenize the microstructure (minimizing segregation), rapidly quench to room temperature, then age at ~500°C for several hours (e.g., 6–12 hours) to trigger fine, controlled precipitation along the lamellar interfaces.
generation.conditions: The heat treatment is designed for applications involving extreme temperature fluctuations (from sub-zero to around 500°C), long-term mechanical loading (relevant to fastener service conditions), room-temperature creep, and exposure to corrosive environments (e.g., salt spray or acidic conditions). Testing can be conducted at room temperature and elevated temperatures with controlled atmosphere (inert or air) and standard strain rates for tensile and creep tests; corrosion tests in a salt spray chamber for standardized durations.
generation.structural_mediator: Fine precipitates forming along lamellar boundaries that refine the microstructure and impede dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding.
generation.mechanism: The aging treatment induces precipitation hardening. The formation of secondary phases at the lamellar interfaces acts to block dislocation movement and enhance load sharing between phases. This refined microstructure can also stabilize against coarsening during temperature fluctuations and reduce pathways for corrosion, while retarding creep by strengthening grain or phase boundaries.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in both yield strength and ductility relative to the as-solidified alloy, with improved creep resistance and corrosion performance. Improvements are expected to be moderate (likely on the order of 10–20% enhancement in key mechanical properties), though the exact magnitude will depend on optimization of the aging parameters.
generation.baseline: As-solidified uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy exhibiting substandard strength and plasticity for industrial fastener applications.
generation.boundary: The improvements are expected to be relevant under operating conditions that include rapid and extreme temperature fluctuations up to ~500°C, continuous mechanical loading with potential for room-temperature creep, and in corrosive environments (e.g., aggressive salt spray conditions). Beyond these boundaries, the stability of the precipitates and the tempered microstructure may need re-assessment.
generation.uncertainty: The precise aging temperature, time, and resultant precipitate size/distribution that yield optimal performance improvements remain to be empirically determined. The balance between strength and plasticity might also be sensitive to slight deviations in the heat treatment cycle.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples from the same production batch. Divide them into a control group (no post-solidification treatment) and an experimental group undergoing the proposed heat treatment (solutionizing at ~1100°C followed by quenching and aging at ~500°C for 6–12 hours). Evaluate mechanical properties (tensile testing for yield strength, ductility, and creep testing at room temperature), thermal cycling tests (to simulate extreme temperature fluctuations), and salt spray corrosion tests. Microstructural analyses (e.g., SEM, TEM, and XRD) will be conducted to confirm the formation and distribution of precipitates.
measurements: Yield strength and tensile ductility from standard tensile tests
Creep strain rate at room temperature under constant load
Microstructural characteristics (precipitate size, distribution, and lamellar spacing) via electron microscopy
Corrosion rate measured via salt spray or electrochemical testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the treated samples do not show a statistically significant improvement (e.g., less than a 10% increase in yield strength and/or ductility) compared to the control group, if the microstructural analyses do not confirm the expected controlled precipitation at the lamellar boundaries, or if the improvements in creep and corrosion resistance are not demonstrable under the tested conditions.
